thread:
maya: Quick note — after landing heuristic_v2 for kernel selection I see a recurring ~3ms hole between NVTX END(allreduce) and NVTX BEGIN(matmul) in nsys captures for embedding-heavy batches.
chris: which hardware/config? TP/PP, batch tokens?
maya: 8xA100, TP=2 PP=1, ~512 tokens per batch, dynamic batching off. RW_KERNEL_SEL=heuristic_v2. Repro steps attached.
priya: can you paste the nvtx snippet? sometimes markers look like gaps but are tool artifacts.
maya: nvprof snippet (trimmed):
```
NVTX: BEGIN allreduce  rank=1
<allreduce kernels...>
NVTX: END allreduce    rank=1
... 3.2 ms idle (no NVTX) ...
NVTX: BEGIN matmul    rank=1
```
maya: I profiled with `nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx` and cross-checked with `nvprof --print-gpu-trace`.
devon: possibilities: (1) real host-side stall (e.g., callback/aggregation), (2) non-blocking GPU ops with NVTX not aligned, (3) stream-affinity change delaying submit. Any explicit cudaSyncs?
maya: runtime doesn't insert explicit syncs. The new kernel selector sometimes chooses variants with `launch_async` that change stream behavior; might introduce a small host-side callback.
chris: try a quick test: add `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` right after allreduce NVTX END and re-run. If gap disappears it's host-side.
maya: did that: gap drops to ~0.1ms, matmul fires immediately.
priya: that indicates host-side enqueue/block. Could be a callback on NCCL completion or a CPU-side memcpy scheduled by the variant. Dump kernel-selector logs?
maya: snippet from /tmp/ks.log: `embedding_matmul -> variant 3 (tile=64x64, launch_async=true)` and `allreduce -> variant 1 (nccl-allreduce, stream=comm_stream)`.
chris: launch_async=true is suspect — variant used to launch on compute_stream synchronously in v1. New variant may post host callbacks.
perf-bot: perf/regressions#4487 created (P2) — median step +1.8ms on embedding workloads since b7f3a. Artifacts attached.
priya: short-term mitigation: force compute_stream launches for embedding matmuls when preceding op used comm_stream (prefer_sync_launch=true). Long-term: selector needs dependency-aware stream assignment.
devon: agree. Also inspect NCCL completion callback path — if it runs aggregation on grpc/comm thread that can block submission. Add NVTX or micro-timer inside the comm callback.
maya: added micro NVTX around comm callback and a CPU timestamp at NVTX END(allreduce) + NVTX BEGIN(matmul). nsys screenshot shows grpc thread doing ~2-3ms of accounting between markers. Link: https://img.company/snapshots/rank1_timeline.png
chris: if accounting is unavoidable, move it off the hot path (async logging) or pre-submit KV-cache prefetch so kernel submission isn't delayed.
priya: I'll draft a short RFC for selector change: add stream-affinity rule and prefer_sync_launch for short-latency adjacency. Include perf traces and micro-timer results.
maya: plan of action: 1) add micro-metric to runtime for this gap, 2) run cluster repro on 3 machines, 3) ship hotfix toggle to rollback kernel selector for embeddings, 4) canary.
perf-bot: buildkite/job/1219: perf smoke with selector=heuristic_v1 shows baseline restored.
maya: OK, pushing hotfix toggle and scheduling canary. Will drop logs in the perf ticket and the RFC. :thumbsup:
chris: if you want bisect help around b7f3a I can take it.
priya: filing RFC now, will ping reviewers.
maya: thanks everyone — updating ticket with artifacts and next steps.
perf-bot: note added to perf/regressions#4487: repro traces, nvprof + nsys captures, candidate hotfix toggle.
